subject: DSR: impact on billing exports and audit trail - invoices vs usage deletion
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@acme-corp.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Billing <billing@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: DSR: what happens to billing exports/invoices when a user requests deletion?

Hi Diego,

We received a Data Subject Request from one of our end users asking for full erasure of their personal data. Two related questions came up on our side and from our auditors:

1) If we comply and delete the user's personal identifiers from our usage logs, will that also remove the record-lines that appear on our billing exports / invoices? Our auditors say we need a persistent invoice trail for accounting.

2) Can Redwood provide a canonical, redacted CSV export suitable for auditors (invoice id, date, product, amount, customer id) that omits the personal identifiers but preserves the transaction-level billing entries? If so, what's the turnaround and format?

I've attached the billing export we pulled (sample) for context.

Thanks — please CC finance/legal as needed.

Samira Khan
Billing Operations Manager | Acme Corp
[sample attached: acme_billing_export_20270428.csv]
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 10:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DSR: what happens to billing exports/invoices when a user requests deletion?

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear note and the sample export. Looping in Marissa from Finance and Neha from Legal/Privacy for formal confirmation.

High-level: what you expect is correct in principle — invoices and the accounting ledger are treated as financial records and we retain them for statutory and audit reasons. Personal identifiers contained in request logs (API keys tied to a user, IPs, etc.) are handled through our DSR process and can be removed. That said, Finance needs to confirm which invoice-level fields are considered PII vs necessary ledger fields.

Quick asks from our side to help Marissa/Neha confirm:
- Which exact columns in your attached CSV contain end-user PII that you want removed? (email, user_id, full_name?)
- Are you requesting a redacted export for audit only, or also an internal permanent redaction from the raw usage logs?
- Is there an active audit / legal hold where you need us to preserve anything in the raw form?

I'll hand off to Marissa for specifics on retention periods and export format.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@acme-corp.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 15:26:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DSR: what happens to billing exports/invoices when a user requests deletion?

Hi Samira — thanks for the sample. From a finance and audit perspective here is Redwood's standard position and the practical steps we take: 

1) Invoices and the accounting ledger: retained.
   - We retain invoice documents, invoice metadata, and the canonical billing ledger for 7 years (standard accounting / tax retention in our jurisdictions).
   - Those records are considered accounting artifacts and are excluded from routine DSR erasure because they are necessary for legal and tax compliance.

2) Usage/request logs and personal identifiers: removable.
   - Per-request logs that contain identifiers tied to an individual (user email, user_id that maps to a natural person, IPs) are treated as personal data and are removable per a DSR once the customer confirms scope.
   - Finance does not require those per-request PII fields to maintain the invoice trail. We keep transaction-level entries (invoice id, line item, date, amount, customer account id) which are not PII for your auditors.

3) Redacted exports for auditors: available.
   - We can produce a canonical, audit-ready export (CSV) containing: invoice_id, invoice_date, line_item_description, quantity, gross_amount, currency, customer_account_id, payment_status.
   - We will exclude or redact user-level columns (user_email, user_id, request_uuid) unless you explicitly request them and have a lawful basis.
   - Typical turnaround: 3 business days for a single-period export. If you need historical exports spanning multiple years expect 5–7 business days depending on size.

4) Accounting hold / active audit: if there is an active legal hold you should notify us immediately. In that case we will suspend deletion of the raw records while preserving a chain-of-custody.

Attached is our internal SOP that describes the export format and the redaction checklist.

Next practical step from your side: confirm the columns you want redacted and whether there is an active hold. Once confirmed we'll queue the export and provide a signed export certificate for your auditors.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Finance Manager, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_billing-retention-sop_v2.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@acme-corp.com>

Cc: Acme Billing <billing@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:41:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DSR: what happens to billing exports/invoices when a user requests deletion?

Thanks Marissa — that's helpful. For our auditors we'd like:
- a redacted export (CSV) with the fields you listed (invoice_id, date, line item, amounts, customer_account_id).
- remove user_email and user_id columns entirely from the export (not just masked).
- confirm that the invoice_id/customer_account_id will remain intact so amounts tie to our ledgers.

There is not currently an active legal hold on this user, but we do have an internal audit scheduled next month that will request supporting docs — so the redacted export will be used for that.

Could you confirm ETA? If you can provide the CSV in 3 business days that will be fine.

Also attaching a small sample we pulled from our system to show which columns map to the ones you listed.

Samira
[sample attached: acme_billing_export_20270428.csv]
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DSR: what happens to billing exports/invoices when a user requests deletion?

Hi all — quick legal note to make the operational guidance actionable: 

- Process we will follow once Acme confirms redaction columns:
  1) Finance creates an export job and sets a preservation flag on the raw billing dataset to prevent automated purges for the specific invoice range.
  2) Engineering runs the export and produces two artifacts: (a) a redacted CSV for auditors (fields per Marissa), and (b) a confirmation that PII fields were removed from production request logs (deletion certificate).
  3) We will provide a signed export metadata manifest (hash + generation timestamp) to preserve chain-of-custody.

- EU residency note: because Acme requested storage within EU, both the redacted export and the deletion operations will be executed against EU-hosted data stores only. If you need a copy delivered outside the EU we will require an approved transfer mechanism.

- Timeline: 3 business days is reasonable for a single-period export; we'll start the clock once Acme confirms the exact columns to omit and whether they want the redaction applied to historical request logs or only to the export artifact.

Please reply with the final column list and whether any legal hold exists. Once confirmed Diego/Marissa will open the export ticket and share the HubSpot export job id.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
